cls: Proton pump inhibitor (substituted benzimidazole; R-enantiomer of lansoprazole)
quick: Erosive esophagitis healing: 60 mg once daily; GERD / maintenance: 30 mg once daily
May be taken without regard to food; swallow whole, do not chew
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Unknown if excreted in milk; use with caution / weigh benefit
Moderate (Child-Pugh B): max 30 mg/day; not studied in severe impairment
Magnesium with long-term use; B12 on prolonged therapy; symptom response
summary: Dexlansoprazole is the R-enantiomer of lansoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor that suppresses gastric acid by irreversibly inhibiting the parietal-cell H+/K+-ATPase. Its dual delayed-release formulation gives two separate drug-release phases, allowing once-daily dosing without regard to meals and prolonged acid control. It is used to heal and maintain erosive esophagitis and to treat symptomatic non-erosive GERD in patients 12 years and older. As with all PPIs, long-term use carries risks of low magnesium, vitamin B12 deficiency, C. difficile diarrhoea, fractures and acute interstitial nephritis.
indications: Healing of all grades of erosive esophagitis (patients 12 years and older)
Maintenance of healed erosive esophagitis and relief of heartburn
Treatment of symptomatic non-erosive gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)

dosage.c: Maintenance of healed EE / heartburn relief

dosage.n: Not studied in severe (Child-Pugh C) impairment

admin: Take once daily without regard to food
Swallow capsule whole; do not chew
Alternatively, open the capsule and sprinkle granules on one tablespoon of applesauce and swallow immediately without chewing, or administer via the approved water/nasogastric methods
Do not crush the delayed-release granules
For symptom control, take at a consistent time each day
moa: Dexlansoprazole is a substituted benzimidazole that, after absorption, accumulates in the acidic parietal-cell canaliculus and is converted to the active sulfenamide, which covalently and irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+-ATPase (the proton pump). This blocks the final common step of acid secretion, markedly reducing both basal and stimulated gastric acid output. Its dual delayed-release design produces two plasma peaks for extended acid suppression.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to dexlansoprazole or any formulation component (reactions include anaphylaxis, angioedema, acute interstitial nephritis)
relative: Concomitant drugs dependent on gastric acidity for absorption
Risk factors for osteoporosis (long-term high-dose use)

preg: Limited human data; lansoprazole-class data have not shown a clear increase in major malformations. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether dexlansoprazole is excreted in human milk; lansoprazole has been detected in animal milk. Consider the benefit of breastfeeding against the potential risk to the infant.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment. Dexlansoprazole pharmacokinetics are not meaningfully altered by reduced renal function. Note the rare class risk of acute interstitial nephritis.
hepatic: In moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B) the maximum dose is 30 mg once daily because of increased exposure. It has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C); use is not recommended without careful consideration.

major: Rilpivirine (contraindicated - PPIs markedly reduce its absorption and efficacy)
Atazanavir, nelfinavir and similar pH-dependent antiretrovirals (reduced levels - avoid)
moderate: Drugs needing gastric acid for absorption: ketoconazole, itraconazole, erlotinib, certain iron salts, atazanavir (reduced absorption)
Methotrexate (PPIs may raise levels, especially high-dose - consider withholding)
Clopidogrel (class caution; effect less than omeprazole)
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to food
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause false-positive chromogranin A elevation; may affect secretin stimulation testing - withhold before testing where relevant

serious: Bone fractures (hip, wrist, spine) with long-term high-dose use
rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis / DRESS

monitoring: Serum magnesium with prolonged therapy or with diuretics/digoxin
Renal function if interstitial nephritis suspected
Reassess need for continued PPI periodically
counsel: Take once a day; you can take it with or without food
Swallow the capsule whole, or sprinkle the granules on applesauce and swallow without chewing
Long-term use can lower magnesium and vitamin B12 and slightly raise fracture risk - use the lowest effective dose
Report watery diarrhoea, muscle cramps, palpitations, or a rash
Heartburn that is new, severe, or with weight loss or trouble swallowing needs medical review
pk: Acid suppression begins on the first day; full effect over a few days of dosing
Dual peaks - approximately 1-2 hours and 4-5 hours after dosing
Approximately 1-2 hours (effect outlasts plasma levels due to irreversible enzyme binding)
Prolonged acid suppression supporting once-daily dosing
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); protect from moisture
pearls: Dual delayed-release design allows once-daily dosing without regard to meals - useful for patients with variable meal timing or nighttime symptoms
It is the R-enantiomer of lansoprazole, the metabolically dominant moiety
Contraindicated with rilpivirine and reduces efficacy of acid-dependent drugs and several antiretrovirals
Reassess long-term use - risks include low magnesium, low B12, fractures, C. difficile and interstitial nephritis
May cause false-positive chromogranin A; hold before neuroendocrine tumour testing
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip the missed one and continue the once-daily schedule - do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is limited experience; dexlansoprazole is not removed by hemodialysis and is well tolerated even at high single doses. Massive overdose is unlikely to be life-threatening; manage symptomatically and supportively. There is no specific antidote.
